Subject: FastPath onboarding — cost & performance tuning sync

Hi Elena / Mike —

Congrats again on selecting Redwood for FastPath. As we move from discovery into hands-on implementation, I want to make sure we’re aligned on the cost/perf tuning work we’ll do during the onboarding window. I’ve attached a short checklist (fastpath-econ-checklist.pdf) and the profiling snapshot from your pilot (initial-profiling.csv).

High-level proposal (30–45 minute working session this week):
- Walk the profiling snapshot (load distribution, typical sequence lengths, percent of streaming vs blocking requests)
- Agree on target SLOs (p95 latency, token cost ceiling, availability)
- Select initial quantization profiles + perf trade-offs to test (safe default + aggressive cost-saving)
- Decide batching thresholds and KV cache TTLs to validate in Stage 1
- Define routing policy for production ramp (latency-primary vs cost-saver path)

Initial recommendations from our side (to discuss):
- Start with two quant profiles: conv-safe-int8 (lower precision but validated for your prompt mix) and conv-econ-4bit (higher savings; regression guard enabled)
- Batch target: 6 requests per batch for median load, with adaptive scaling up to 20 for spikes (respecting p95 latency guardrails)
- KV cache TTL: 30s for short-session chat flows; 300s for multi-turn customers that reuse context often
- Routing: route to low-latency pool during business hours; fallback to cost-saver pool if queue depth > 30% of capacity or latency breaches

Can we lock 45 minutes tomorrow at 10:00am PT? If that time doesn't work, propose two alternatives and we’ll adapt.

Thanks — looking forward to a concise plan we can run in the first two weeks of onboarding.

Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Elena, good questions — I pulled a few implementation-first notes together ahead of the call. Wanted to capture them here so the meeting is focused.

Short answers:
- Fidelity: conv-econ-4bit is higher-risk for certain instruction-style prompts. We recommend an A/B test window where 10% of production traffic is routed to the 4-bit profile behind a regression check set (your contract synthesis prompts plus additional edge cases). If eval metrics (ROUGE-like similarity + phantom-entity rate) deviate beyond threshold, auto-failover to conv-safe-int8.

- Routing & SLA: both pools serve the same model weights; the difference is runtime kernels and batch sizing. The cost-saver path uses a higher batching target and more aggressive fusion kernels which can add 50–120ms median token latency under some conditions but generally preserve token outputs. We'll configure the routing policy as:
  - primary: latency-pool (single-token latency optimized)
  - fallback: cost-saver pool (batching-heavy)
  - trigger: fallback when p95 token-latency > SLA_THRESHOLD OR queue length > 0.3 * pool_capacity
  - safety: circuit breaker that reverts routing to latency-pool if error rate increases > 0.5% over baseline

- Monitoring / alerts (first 14 days):
  - token-level p50/p95 latency per route (alert if p95 > target)
  - batch size distribution (alert if median batch size drops below expected range — indicates traffic skew)
  - KV cache hit ratio (alert if < 60% for flows expected to reuse context)
  - regression checkset pass rate for 4-bit profile (alert if pass rate < 98%)
  - model-generation error rate (increases > 0.5% triggers automatic rollback)

Implementation knobs we’ll exercise in Stage 1 (week 1):
- Quant profiles: conv-safe-int8 (default), conv-econ-4bit (guarded A/B)
- Batch controls: target_mean_batch = 6, max_batch = 20, time_window_ms = 20 for adaptive batching
- KV cache: per-route TTLs (30s for short chats, 300s for multi-turn), prefetch warm keys for known workflows
- Tracing: attach per-request trace_id to logs and align with your observability; we’ll instrument a sampling rate of 10% to start

I’ll drop these notes into the shared Drive folder and include a short checklist in the calendar invite. See HubSpot deal ZPH-2028-045 for milestone gating and acceptance criteria.

—Karthik
